With the logo removed you would still know this is a kiln product. The lower half falls back to a familiar numbered-steps list beside a phone mockup.
evidence.proof: The hero board is operable: Loading, Firing, Cooling and Out each redraw the curve and the readout (Firing: '1,770°F and climbing toward cone 6'). It only shows status, though. The core job, claiming a shelf, sits in the phone mockup about 1830px down at 1440 and about 2890px down at 390. The numbers disagree across artifacts: the Loading readout says 'Three spots are still open' while the phone shows four Open spots for the same firing (Glaze cone 6, claims close Tue 2pm), and Out says 'Fourteen members' for a 12-spot kiln shared by about five names.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Nobody asks “is it out yet?”' states an outcome, followed by the bold line 'Kilnlog is a kiln booking app for community pottery studios.' and the three jobs. The note under the CTA ('Free for 30 days, for studio owners. Members don't sign up here; their studio invites them.') settles who acts. A stranger could repeat it.
evidence.fit: The member path is strong: the hero sample kiln, before/after rows and the 'For members' note. The owner path is thin: one 'For studio owners' paragraph beside the log ('You pay for Kilnlog and invite your members') with no view of what the owner controls (scheduling firings, updating status, shelf rules), which is where 'trust it with their schedule' would be won. The tone is warm (terracotta band, pot icons with chop-mark initials) and the 'no figures' constraint is respected ('In use at three community studios since spring').
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is a kiln cross-section with three shelves, coil walls, pot glyphs (bowl, mug, vase, plate) and chop-mark initials (MR, JO, AK), and the chamber glows orange in Firing. The sticky-note sheet with scrawled 'who took my spot??', the mono 'Sample...' labels and the clay colour band give it a recognisable face. The structure (hero, problem, table, CTA band) is conventional, and the display serif resolves to DejaVu Serif first, which reads close to default.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the sample kiln is the right half of the first screen and does the core job: tapped '+ Open' on shelf 1 and got 'You claimed shelf 1, spot 2. 8 of 12 spots claimed.' The message card changed to 'Kilnlog will tell you and the 7 other members'. In Out the card turns green: 'message sent ... Your piece is on shelf 2, spot 3'. The numbers stay consistent: 7 of 12 claimed in the hero matches the 'Thursday bisque, Loading, 7 of 12 claimed' row in the firing log below.
evidence.craft: Probe axe shows 0 violations at 390 and 1440, and there is no overflow. The hierarchy is clear: the dark card on terracotta, mono labels, chips. Minor issues: the open mobile menu panel leaves a sliver of the H1 visible between the header bar and the panel (390, tapped Menu at the top), and the display face falls back to DejaVu Serif, which looks heavy and generic in this render. At 1440 the door section's left column (sheet plus three stacked chat bubbles) runs long against the before/after table.
evidence.mobile: 390: H1, lead, full-width CTA and the top of the sample kiln (label, Reset, stage tabs, status, message card, shelf 1) all fit in the first screen. The stage tabs are 81x44, Reset is 70x44 and spot buttons are 70x52. The before/after table is recomposed into labelled 'Before / Kilnlog' rows and the log into cards with a 'Spots:' prefix, not shrunk. The Menu button opens a panel with 44px links, Escape closes it, and tapping 'Firing log' closes it and scrolls. On the phone the status line sits about 150 to 250px above the lower shelves, but the 'YOU' pot appears in place.
evidence.honesty: Every artifact is labelled at its top: 'Sample kiln, written for this page', 'Sample sheet and chat, written for this page', 'Sample week, written for this page'. The CTA note says before the click that the trial is free for 30 days and for studio owners. The only social claim is the brief's own 'three community studios since spring'.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. Claim, move ('You moved to shelf 2, spot 3 ... In this sample you hold one spot') and give back ('You gave back shelf 1, spot 2. 7 of 12') all work. Tapping a spot while Out shows the guard 'Shelf spots can only be claimed while the kiln is loading. Press Loading to try it.' Reset restores 7 of 12 and the default message. Stages switch the chamber colour and open spots become 'Empty'. Tab order goes through the CTA, Reset, the four stages and each open spot with a visible outline plus ring. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Lines are tight and from the studio: 'Squeeze your name into a gap on the sheet and hope nobody writes over it', 'the group chat goes back to talking about pots', 'Still too hot to open. Members can see that from home.' Buttons are consistent ('Start your free 30-day trial' everywhere). Kiln vocabulary is lighter than A's (no cones), and the owner copy is generic.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the specific outcome headline, the one-line definition, the CTA with the owners/members note and the operable sample kiln (7 of 12 claimed, message preview) are all in one viewport. 390: the headline, definition, CTA and the kiln card down to shelf 1 with tappable '+ Open' are all above 844px.

problems: The studio owner, who pays, gets one paragraph: nothing shows scheduling firings, setting shelf rules or updating status, which is what earns schedule trust
The display face falls back to DejaVu Serif first and reads heavy and close to default, weakening the type's point of view
Small polish issues: the open mobile menu leaves a sliver of the H1 between header and panel, and the door section's left column runs long at 1440

reason: B puts the product's core job (claim a shelf spot, watch the stage, get the 'it's out' message) in the first screen at both 1440 and 390. Its numbers hold together across the page, its tables are recomposed for the phone, and every state I reached is handled. A has the richer craft voice (firing curve, glaze palette) and a much better owner section, but its claim demo is buried and its numbers contradict each other. A version of A with the shelf claim promoted into the hero and the counts reconciled, or a B that still lacked an owner path in the buyer's reading, would change my mind.
